channel.title: National Public Radio (NPR) - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from National Public Radio (NPR) (npr.org)

item.title: ICE deployments created chaos for cities and cost them millions, NPR analysis finds
item.description: Local leaders report already-strapped police departments racked up overtime bills in the millions while others report a multi-million dollar hit to business during the worst ICE surges.

item.title: Trump delivers farmers another financial blow with Iran war
item.description: Some of President Trump's policies, the latest being the war in Iran, are testing his support among farmers who are being burdened with higher costs.

item.title: Kim vows to 'irreversibly' cement North Korea's nuclear status
item.description: In his speech, Kim expressed pride in the country's rapid expansion of nuclear weapons and missiles in recent years, calling it the "right" choice.

item.title: Iran fires more missiles at Israel and rejects Trump's talk as 'fake news' for markets
item.description: Israeli health officials said Iranian missiles struck four sites across Israel Tuesday, including central Tel Aviv, injuring at least six people. Iranian authorities also said a gas supply line in southwest Iran was struck overnight.

item.title: Before running for Congress, Bobby Pulido was a Tejano music icon
item.description: Pulido has been a mainstay of Tejano music —a genre blending traditional regional Mexican elements with country, pop and conjunto influences — for more than three decades.

item.title: Mumford & Sons: Tiny Desk Concert
item.description: The British folk-rock band shares world-weary anthems to growing older, weathering the innumerable blows of life and coming out on the other side, hopefully a little wiser.

item.title: How Trump's Iran war objectives have shifted over time
item.description: Here is a reminder of some of what he has said - and where the US is now.

item.title: Are you sure you know what 'gaslighting' is?
item.description: Therapists say we're overusing the word. Here's what it actually means — and what the Ingrid Bergman film that helped birth the word can teach us about it.

item.title: Your data is everywhere. The government is buying it without a warrant
item.description: Data brokers buy up huge amounts of information from cell phones and browsers to sell for targeted advertising. But the government, including ICE, also buys the data.

item.title: A shelter village provides a bridge to permanent housing
item.description: Shelter villages offer temporary and private places for the unhoused to sleep and store belongings. One of the newest, The Bridge, opened recently in central Illinois.

item.title: They gave her business a lifeline, then froze all her money
item.description: A murky corner of the financial world is now the fastest-growing source of funding for small businesses. One state, Connecticut, had given these lenders unusual power. That may be about to change.

item.title: Iran rejects Trump's proposal to end the war and lays out 5 conditions, state TV says
item.description: Iran submitted a counterproposal that includes safeguards against future attacks against Iran and the country's right to "sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz," Iranian state Press TV reported.

item.title: Yep, a mom's COVID shot during pregnancy protects her baby, a large study finds
item.description: A 3-year study published in Pediatrics examined newborns in Norway. It found a clear benefit for the baby when mom gets a COVID vaccination during pregnancy.

item.title: A 92-year-old judge will take on the Maduro case. What do we know about him?
item.description: Former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro heads to court again this week. The judge overseeing this case is longtime federal Judge Alvin Hellerstein. At 92 years old, Hellerstein is older than the average age of a federal judge by more than 20 years.

item.title: DHS funding deal on shaky ground as Trump and Democrats both decline to embrace it
item.description: After weeks of start and stop negotiations between Congressional Democrats and the White House, there's an emerging proposal to fund the majority of DHS and tackle ICE enforcement funding separately.
